chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ismail ibn Umar, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who entered a town and found meat there, not knowing whether it was slaughtered or dead. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should throw it into the fire; so whatever shrivels is slaughtered, and whatever expands is dead.'

key_terms.انْبَسَطَ: Expands (indicates mayyit status in this context)
key_terms.انْقَبَضَ: Shrivels/contracts (indicates halal status in this context)
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: Slaughtered (animal properly slaughtered according to Islamic law)
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: Dead (animal that died naturally or was not slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: How to distinguish between slaughtered and dead meat using fire?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a practical empirical test (istishhād) for determining the ritual purity of meat when the method of slaughter is unknown, a common issue in early Islamic communities. By observing whether the meat shrivels (indicating proper blood drainage via dhakī) or expands (indicating retained blood via mayyit), the Imam provides a tangible criterion for consumption. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing doubt (shakk) through observable physical signs in matters of dietary law.
